title: Bankruptcy and Deceased Notices, Client Recalls and Return Reasons (Placed Consumer Accounts)
content:
Compliance manual section for **Placed Consumer Accounts** on protected-status notices, client recalls, and the reason recorded when an account is returned to the client.

## Section text

**1. Bankruptcy notice.** A bankruptcy notice is recorded only when the caller provides the bankruptcy case number, which is stored as the notice's reference number. A caller who only says they are thinking of filing, or have consulted an attorney, has given no bankruptcy notice.

**2. Deceased notice.** A deceased notice is recorded only when the caller provides the death certificate number, stored as the notice's reference number. Afterwards Ridgeline speaks about the debt only with the personal representative of the estate.

**3. Where and how often.** Each notice type is recorded once per account, on every open placed account of the consumer.

**4. Effect of a notice.** From the notice onward no collection activity takes place and no payment is solicited or posted on the account; a plan or settlement on it is cancelled or withdrawn under its own rules.

**5. Return after a notice.** The account is returned to the client with close reason bankruptcy filed within the stage's bankruptcy return time, in business days after the notice's date, or with close reason consumer deceased within the stage's deceased return time, in business days after the notice's date; a live tradeline is deleted under the credit reporting rule.

**6. Client recall.** A client recall is returned with close reason client recall within the stage's recall processing time, in business days after the recall request is accepted.

**7. Several reasons on one day.** When more than one return reason applies on the same day, the reason recorded follows this order:

| Priority | Close reason recorded |
|---|---|
| 1 | Identity theft confirmed |
| 2 | Bankruptcy filed |
| 3 | Consumer deceased |
| 4 | Unverifiable dispute |
| 5 | Client recall |
| 6 | Term expired |

## What the caller must supply

| Notice | Supplied by the caller | Recorded |
|---|---|---|
| Bankruptcy | The bankruptcy case number | Yes |
| Bankruptcy | Only a statement of intending to file or of having seen an attorney | No |
| Deceased | The death certificate number | Yes |

## Hypothetical cases

*Invented situations.*

- A consumer with three open placed accounts gives a bankruptcy case number. A bankruptcy notice is recorded on each of the three accounts, once each, and no payment is posted on them from then on.
- On the same day a client recall and an unverifiable-dispute return both apply to one account. The close reason recorded is unverifiable dispute, which ranks above client recall.
- A relative calls to report a death but has no death certificate number. No deceased notice is recorded.
